scenes.title: Sunlight is secretly colourful
scenes.narration: Sunlight looks plain white or yellow. But it has a secret! Hiding inside it are all the colors of the rainbow, mixed together like a bag of colorful sweets.

scenes.title: The air is full of tiny bits
scenes.narration: The air around you is not empty. It is full of teeny tiny bits, far too small to see. When sunlight rushes through the air, it bumps into those tiny bits.

scenes.title: Blue is extra bouncy
scenes.narration: Red light zooms straight through. But blue light is extra bouncy! It ricochets off the tiny bits and scatters all over the sky, like a bouncy ball in a playground.

scenes.title: Blue from everywhere
scenes.narration: All that bouncing blue light comes to your eyes from every direction. So when you look up, the whole big sky looks blue!

scenes.title: Why sunsets glow
scenes.narration: At sunset the Sun is low, so its light takes a long trip through the air. Most of the blue bounces away before it reaches you. Only red and orange are left, so the sky glows!

draw.s: a long trip through the air

quiz.question: What is sunlight really made of?
quiz.explanation: Sunlight hides every color of the rainbow inside it.

quiz.question: Which color bounces around the most in the air?
quiz.explanation: Blue light is the bounciest, so it fills the whole sky.

quiz.question: Why is the sunset red and orange?
options: The light travels far and the blue bounces away
quiz.explanation: After a long trip through the air, only red and orange are left.

lessons.title: Where does rain come from?
lessons.subtitle: The water that goes round and round

scenes.title: The Sun warms the sea
scenes.narration: Puddles, rivers and seas are full of water. When the warm Sun shines on them, some water turns into a very light, invisible mist called vapor. It floats up, up, up into the sky.

draw.s: water goes up as invisible vapor

scenes.title: Clouds are made
scenes.narration: High in the sky the air is cold. The vapor cools down and turns back into tiny drops of water. Billions of them huddle together, and that is what a cloud is!

scenes.title: Drops get heavy
scenes.narration: The little drops bump into each other and join up. They grow big and heavy, until the cloud cannot hold them any more. Down they fall as rain!

scenes.title: Water goes home
scenes.narration: The rain fills the rivers, and the rivers flow all the way back to the sea. Then the Sun warms the water, and it starts all over again.

scenes.title: A giant circle
scenes.narration: Up as vapor, together as clouds, down as rain, and back again. The water is going round and round, and it has been doing it for millions of years!

quiz.question: What makes water float up into the sky?
quiz.explanation: The Sun's warmth turns water into vapor that floats up.

quiz.question: What is a cloud made of?
quiz.explanation: A cloud is billions of tiny water drops huddled together.

quiz.question: Where does the rain water go after it falls?
options: Into rivers and back to the sea
quiz.explanation: Rivers carry it back to the sea, and the cycle starts again.

scenes.title: Sun and rain together
scenes.narration: Rainbows appear when the Sun shines while it is raining. The sunshine and the little raindrops hang in the air at the same time. That is the recipe!

scenes.title: A drop bends the light
scenes.narration: Sunlight slips inside a raindrop, and something magic happens. The water bends the light, and the colors hidden inside begin to separate.

scenes.title: Colours spread out
scenes.narration: Every color bends by a different amount. Red bends a little, and purple bends the most. So the colors fan out and come back out of the drop in a neat order.

draw.s: each colour bends a different amount

scenes.title: Millions of drops
scenes.narration: There are millions of raindrops in the sky, and each one sends colors to your eyes. All together they paint a giant, curved band of color across the sky.

scenes.title: Always the same order
scenes.narration: Red is always on top, then orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. To see a rainbow, stand with the Sun behind you and look at the rain in front of you.

draw.s: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple
Sun behind you, rain in front!

quiz.question: When do rainbows appear?
options: When the Sun shines and it rains
quiz.explanation: You need sunshine and raindrops at the same time.

quiz.question: What do raindrops do to sunlight?
options: Bend it and spread out its colors
quiz.explanation: Each color bends by a different amount, so they spread out.

quiz.question: Which color is on top of a rainbow?
quiz.explanation: Red is always at the top and purple at the bottom.

scenes.title: Storm clouds
scenes.narration: Sometimes big dark storm clouds roll in. Inside them, tiny bits of ice and water droplets are zooming up and down, rubbing and bumping into each other.

scenes.title: Sparks gather
scenes.narration: All that rubbing is like rubbing a balloon on your hair. It builds up static electricity! The top of the cloud collects plus charge, and the bottom collects minus charge.

draw.s: tiny bits of ice rub and bump

scenes.title: Zap!
scenes.narration: When there is too much electricity, it has to go somewhere. It makes a giant spark that leaps across the sky or down to the ground. That spark is lightning!

scenes.title: Boom!
scenes.narration: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun! It heats the air so fast that the air bursts outward with a giant BOOM. That booming sound is thunder.

draw.s: The air gets super hot, then BOOM!

scenes.title: Light is faster than sound
scenes.narration: Light travels much faster than sound. So you see the flash first, and hear the thunder later. Count the seconds in between to know how far away the storm is!

draw.s: Light zooms: you see the flash first
Sound is slower: the thunder comes later

quiz.question: What is lightning?
quiz.explanation: Built-up static electricity jumps as a giant spark.

quiz.question: What makes the sound of thunder?
quiz.explanation: The air heats so fast it bursts outward with a BOOM.

quiz.question: Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
options: Your eyes are faster than your ears
quiz.explanation: Light travels much faster than sound.
